claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies can be modified by cryo-rolling and annealing to improve both strength and tensile ductility.
Cryo-rolling and annealing produce a hierarchical microstructure containing fine lamellar regions and ultrafine grains.
The hierarchical microstructure enhances strength-ductility synergy through a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
The hierarchical microstructure enhances strength-ductility synergy through a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Deformation twinning contributes to the proposed strength-ductility enhancement.
The intervention will increase yield strength relative to the as-cast or conventionally processed lamellar baseline.
The intervention will increase elongation to failure relative to the as-cast or conventionally processed lamellar baseline.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength of approximately 1400 MPa.
The processed alloy will have an elongation to failure of approximately 14%.
The approximately 1400 MPa yield strength and 14% elongation are room-temperature tensile properties.
The resulting hierarchical microstructure and strength-ductility synergy are sensitive to cryo-rolling and annealing parameters.
The exact relationship between the hierarchical microstructure and strength-ductility synergy is not fully understood.
Failure of both yield strength and elongation to improve after formation of the hierarchical microstructure would falsify the hypothesis.
